# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to transmit the manual’s color code and lookup table to Deaf, who can then speak the required color to Blind. I’ll use gesture positions as a compact code: the four legend gestures represent blue, green, yellow, and red in that order; each row then gives its display number followed by outputs for blue, green, and yellow light.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👏", "☝", "🤟", "🖖", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👏", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👏", "🤟", "☝", "🤟", "👏", "🖖", "🤟", "🖖", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual, obtain Deaf's observations, and tell me the exact wire position to cut: 1, 2, or 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb observations: display 8. Light green. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please relay the manual's required action and any needed wire choice to Blind.

The manual maps display 8 with green light to red. Among the wires, wire 1 is red, so Deaf must relay “cut wire 1” to Blind. I’ll use the previously established color symbols and separator, with one raised finger indicating wire 1.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖖", "👏", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have no data. After receiving Deaf's observations, send me exactly one safe wire number: 1, 2, or 3. Do not ask me to infer colours or markings.

The required color is red, and the red wire is position 1. Deaf can see the single gesture for wire 1 and relay that number by voice to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 8, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please apply the manual and send me the exact wire position to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact required action directly to Blind, including which wire or control to use. Do not rely on gestures.

The manual requires red for display 8 with green light, and wire 1 is red. I cannot speak, so I’ll signal Deaf the established wire-1 instruction; Deaf can then state the exact action aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have not received your manual instruction. Please state the single wire position to cut now, based on display 8, green light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.
Deaf says to Mute: Your gestures are not an agreed code. Speak the manual's exact action aloud to Blind, including the control or wire, so Blind can act safely.

The manual yields red for display 8 with green light, and the red wire is wire 1. I cannot speak, so I can only show Deaf the standard one-finger signal for wire 1, which Deaf can then say aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the manual result directly to me: cut wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3. The observed state is display 8, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.
Deaf says to Mute: Use this code for your next reply: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 👏 means cut or act. Send only the needed symbols, in order, using these meanings.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👏]

The manual result is red, and the red wire is wire 1. Deaf has now provided an agreed gesture code, so I will send the wire-1 symbol followed by the action symbol for Deaf to relay aloud to Blind.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | blue | yellow | red |
| 7 | red | blue | yellow |
| 8 | yellow | red | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please have Deaf relay the confirmed manual result to me as plain speech: cut wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3.

The confirmed manual result remains wire 1: display 8 with green light requires red, and wire 1 is red. Deaf’s agreed code uses ☝ for wire 1 and 👏 for the action, so I will send both for Deaf to relay as plain speech.

```code
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏"])
```
